Sheaf of modules

 Home Mathematics Area of mathematics Geometry and topology Algebraic geometry Ringed space
OurBigBook.com Words: 9k Articles: 167
For a ringed space (X,OX​), a sheaf of OX​-modules is a sheaf F such that every F(U) is an OX​(U)-module and restriction maps preserve scalar multiplication.
The underlying object is a Sheaf (mathematics) with compatible local module actions.

Internal Hom sheaf (HomOX​​(F,G))

Words: 54
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
For sheaves of modules F,G on a ringed space, the internal Hom sheaf assigns to an open U the module of sheaf morphisms F∣U​→G∣U​ respecting OU​. Compatible morphisms glue, so this is a sheaf. Its global sections are precisely the global module-sheaf morphisms. For a locally free sheaf F of finite rank it is F∨⊗G.

Local system

Words: 26
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
A local system is a locally constant sheaf of modules, for example the integral cohomology of fibres of a smooth proper family of compact complex manifolds. Parallel continuation around loops gives its monodromy representation.

Rational section of a sheaf of modules (Rat(F)=lim​U dense open​Γ(U,F))

Words: 347 Articles: 4
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
A rational section is a section on a dense open subset, with two representatives identified when they agree on a common dense open subset. Intersecting representatives' domains defines addition. Multiplication by a similarly represented rational function on an algebraic variety makes these classes a module over the ring Rat(X). For an irreducible variety, this ring is its function field.

Rational principal part (Rat(F)/FP​)

Words: 242 Articles: 2
Rational section of a sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
For a locally free sheaf on an irreducible variety, the stalk inclusion identifies sections regular near P inside its rational sections. The quotient records the obstruction to regularity at that point. This definition does not assume a nonsingular point or a discrete valuation parameter.

Rational principal-parts resolution on an algebraic curve (0→F→R(F)→P(F)→0)

Words: 203 Articles: 1
Rational principal part OurBigBook.com
On an irreducible algebraic curve, let R(F) be the constant rational-section sheaf and put P(F)(U)=⨁P∈U​Rat(F)/FP​. Every open subset is quasi-compact, so compatible finite-support families glue with finite support. Its stalk at P is the displayed rational-principal-part quotient. A rational section is regular outside finitely many points, making its principal-part map well defined. The resulting sequence is stalkwise exact. Both right-hand sheaves are flasque, and consequently H1(X,F) is the cokernel of the global principal-part map and Hq(X,F)=0 for q≥2. The curve and Zariski-topology hypotheses distinguish finite support here from locally finite pole sets in complex analysis.
Affine principal-parts interpolation for a locally free sheaf
Words: 99
Rational principal-parts resolution on an algebraic curve OurBigBook.com
Let X be an irreducible affine curve, A=k[X], K=FracA, and F=M be locally free. Given finitely many classes in MK​/MmP​​, choose one nonzero a∈A clearing denominators of representatives. The ring A/(a) is Artinian and is the product of its finitely many local factors. Hence M/aM≅⨁P∈V(a)​(M/aM)mP​​. Prescribe avP​ modulo aMmP​​ at the requested points and zero at the other zeros of a. Lift this tuple to w∈M; the section w/a has exactly the requested rational principal parts and no others. This proves surjectivity without assuming the curve is nonsingular.

Stalk inclusion into rational sections of a locally free sheaf (FP​↪Rat(F))

Words: 55
Rational section of a sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
On an irreducible variety, every nonempty open subset is dense, so a germ determines a rational section. For a locally free sheaf, this map is injective: a local section which vanishes on a dense open has all its regular coefficient functions zero, hence is zero. Local freeness is important; a section of a torsion sheaf can vanish generically without having zero germ.

Coherent analytic sheaf (F a coherent OX​-module)

Words: 49
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
On a complex manifold, a sheaf of modules over the sheaf of holomorphic functions is coherent analytic if it is locally finitely generated and the kernel of every morphism Or→F is locally finitely generated. The structure sheaf and locally free finite-rank sheaves are examples. Cartan theorem B gives vanishing of their higher sheaf cohomology on a Stein manifold.

Dual of a sheaf (F∨=HomOX​​(F,OX​))

Words: 57
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
The dual is the sheaf of modules whose sections on U are module-sheaf morphisms F∣U​→OU​. For a locally free sheaf of finite rank, the dual is locally free of the same rank and the natural double-dual map is an isomorphism. General coherent sheaves need not have this property: a skyscraper at a point of positive-dimensional projective space has zero ordinary sheaf dual.

Injective sheaf of modules

Words: 93 Articles: 1
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
On a ringed space (X,OX​), an injective module sheaf is an injective object in the category of sheaves of modules over OX​. Its defining extension property concerns module-sheaf morphisms; it is distinct from injectivity solely in the category of sheaves of abelian groups.

Injective module sheaves are flasque

Words: 56
Injective sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
For opens U⊆V⊆X, there is a monomorphism between the extensions by zero of OU​ and OV​. Morphisms from these sheaves into an injective sheaf of modules I identify with sections on U and V, respectively. The injective object extension property therefore makes the restriction I(V)→I(U) surjective, proving that I is flasque. The argument applies to any ringed space.

Stalk of a sheaf (Fx​)

Words: 347 Articles: 7
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
The stalk Fx​ is the direct limit of F(U) over neighborhoods U of x. A morphism of sheaves is an isomorphism or forms an exact sequence exactly when it does so on every stalk.

Costalk (ix!​E)

Words: 35
Stalk of a sheaf OurBigBook.com
The derived costalk at x is ix!​E, where ix​:{x}↪X. It computes local cohomology supported at x. On an oriented N-manifold the constant sheaf has costalk Q[−N], whose cohomology is in degree N.

Stalk functor for presheaves of sets (F↦Fx​)

Words: 93 Articles: 1
Stalk of a sheaf OurBigBook.com
For presheaves of sets, Fx​=lim​U∋x​F(U). This functor preserves finite limits because the neighborhood system is filtered and filtered colimits commute with finite limits in sets. Its right adjoint sends a set S to the presheaf taking the value S on opens containing x and the singleton on other opens.

Joint stalk functor on sheaves of sets (F↦(Fx​)x∈X​)

Words: 49
Stalk functor for presheaves of sets OurBigBook.com
The joint stalk functor Sh(X)→SetX is faithful: equality of germs makes two images of a section locally equal, and the sheaf uniqueness axiom makes them globally equal. Its right adjoint is the product of the set-valued skyscraper sheaves at all points. The Beck comonadicity theorem then makes the joint stalk functor comonadic.

Skyscraper sheaf

Words: 123 Articles: 1
Stalk of a sheaf OurBigBook.com
For a point inclusion i:{x}↪X and an abelian group A, the skyscraper sheaf i∗​A has sections A on opens containing x and zero on other opens. Its restriction maps are identities or maps to zero. If A=0, its nonzero stalks occur at every point of the closure {x}​: exactly those points whose every neighbourhood contains x. Thus the familiar assertion that only the stalk at x is nonzero requires x to be a closed point. It is always flasque, giving the stated skyscraper sheaf cohomology.

Skyscraper sheaf cohomology (H0(X,i∗​A)=A,Hi>0(X,i∗​A)=0)

Words: 39
Skyscraper sheaf OurBigBook.com
For any point inclusion i:{x}↪X, the skyscraper sheaf i∗​A has restriction maps that are identities or maps to zero. It is flasque, so its higher sheaf cohomology vanishes and its global sections are A. This requires no assumption that x is closed.

Stalk of a sheaf OurBigBook.com
The germ sx​ of a section s∈F(U) is its image in the stalk of a sheaf Fx​. It is zero exactly when s restricts to zero on some neighbourhood of x.

Sheafification

Words: 89 Articles: 2
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
Sheafification associates a sheaf to a presheaf without changing its stalks and is universal among morphisms from that presheaf to sheaves.

Universal property of sheafification (Hom(F+,H)≅Hompre​(F,H))

Words: 29
Sheafification OurBigBook.com
Every presheaf morphism from F to a sheaf H factors uniquely through the canonical sheafification map. Local representatives give local images in H, and the sheaf gluing axiom makes their union unique.

Sheafification by locally representable germs (F+(U)⊆∏x∈U​Fx​)

Words: 39
Sheafification OurBigBook.com
For a presheaf, take families of elements of its stalks which near each point are the germs of one presheaf section. Pointwise operations and restriction make these families into a sheaf. The map sending a section to all its germs is its sheafification map.

Extension by zero (j!​F)

Words: 43
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
For an open inclusion j:U↪X, extension by zero is the sheaf j!​F whose stalk equals Fx​ on U and zero outside U. Its sections are local sections on U whose support is closed in the ambient open set.

Quasi-coherent sheaf

Words: 967 Articles: 16
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
A sheaf of modules on a scheme is quasi-coherent when every affine chart SpecA restricts it to the sheaf associated with an A-module. On an affine scheme it is determined by its module of global sections.

Kernels of quasi-coherent sheaf morphisms (ker(M→N)=ker(M→N)​)

Words: 48
Quasi-coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
On an affine scheme, a morphism between quasi-coherent sheaves is determined by the induced map on global sections, because its maps on principal open subsets are their localizations. Exactness of localization gives the displayed identity. Thus the kernel sheaf of a morphism between quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent on an arbitrary scheme, by applying the affine argument locally. No finite generation is needed.

Affine module sheaf (M(D(f))=Mf​)

Words: 159 Articles: 1
Quasi-coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
For an affine variety with coordinate ring A and an A-module M, localization defines sections on principal open subsets by the displayed formula. Restrictions are the natural localization maps. Equivalently, a section is a family of stalk values which locally come from one fraction m/fr. These data form a quasi-coherent sheaf, with global sections M and stalk MmP​​ at P. Sheaf tensor products correspond to tensor products over A; pullback of a sheaf of modules corresponds to extension of scalars, and affine direct image to restriction of scalars.

Coherence of an affine module sheaf (M coherent⟺M finitely generated)

Words: 87
Affine module sheaf OurBigBook.com
For a Noetherian ring A, a finitely generated module M has a finite presentation of a module, and kernels of maps from finite free modules to M are finitely generated. Its affine module sheaf is therefore a coherent sheaf. Conversely, if M is coherent, choose a finite principal open subset cover on which its section modules are finitely generated. Lift their finitely many generators to numerators in M. The submodule generated by these numerators becomes all of M on every chart, and hence is all of M: its quotient has zero localization at every point. This proves finite generation without assuming that global sections preserve arbitrary sheaf surjections.

Quasi-coherent sheaves are closed under extensions

Words: 106
Quasi-coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
In 0→F→G→E→0, assume the outer sheaves are quasi-coherent. On an affine open, any section of E has local lifts to G on a finite principal cover. Their differences are a Čech cocycle in the module defining F. Exactness of the unit-ideal localization Čech complex makes this cocycle a coboundary, so adjusted lifts glue. Thus sections are exact on the affine open and on every principal open in it. Comparing the resulting sequences after localization, the outer isomorphisms force the middle localization map to be an isomorphism. Hence G is associated with its global-section module and is quasi-coherent.

Global-section localization for quasi-coherent sheaves (Γ(SpecA,F)a​≃Γ(D(a),F))

Words: 95
Quasi-coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
Choose a finite cover of an affine scheme by principal opens on which the quasi-coherent sheaf is associated with a module. The sheaf gluing axiom expresses global sections as the kernel of the difference map from the finite product of chart sections to the finite product of overlap sections. Localization commutes with kernels and finite products. Localizing at a therefore gives the same kernel for the cover intersected with D(a), proving the formula. The principal-open formulas identify the sheaf with that associated with its global-section module; no finite-generation hypothesis on the module is needed.

Affine module-sheaf equivalence (A-Mod≃QCoh(X))

Words: 41
Quasi-coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
On an affine variety or affine scheme with coordinate ring A, the global section functor and M↦M are inverse equivalences between modules and quasi-coherent sheaves. On every principal open subset, sections are the appropriate localization of a module. Localization detects exactness at maximal ideals, so these functors are exact even for modules which are not finitely generated.

Torsion-free sheaf

Words: 38
Quasi-coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
On an integral scheme, a quasi-coherent sheaf is torsion-free when its module on every affine chart is a torsion-free module over that chart's integral domain. It embeds into its generic fibre. Therefore a torsion-free sheaf with zero generic fibre is zero; locally free sheaves and their subsheaves are torsion-free.

Vanishing of quasi-coherent cohomology on an affine scheme (Hi>0(SpecA,M)=0)

Words: 44
Quasi-coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
Every quasi-coherent sheaf on an affine scheme has zero higher sheaf cohomology. Together with the equivalence between modules and quasi-coherent sheaves on an affine scheme, this makes affine varieties the basic acyclic pieces for computing cohomology. An affine open cover of a separated scheme has affine finite intersections, so the acyclic cover theorem identifies its Čech cohomology with sheaf cohomology.

Coherent sheaf

Words: 399 Articles: 7
Quasi-coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
On a locally Noetherian scheme, a coherent sheaf is a quasi-coherent sheaf that is locally associated with a finitely generated module. Kernels, cokernels, and finite direct sums of coherent sheaves remain coherent.

Globally generated sheaf (Γ(X,F)⊗OX​↠F)

Words: 80
Coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
A sheaf of modules is globally generated when the evaluation map from its global sections is surjective. Equivalently, the germs of global sections span each stalk as a module over the local ring. For a coherent sheaf on a projective variety, every sufficiently positive twist is globally generated: embed the variety in projective space, present its direct-image sheaf as a quotient of a finite sum of O(−a), twist until those line bundles are globally generated, and restrict their generating sections to the variety.

Stalkwise isomorphic coherent sheaves need not be isomorphic

Words: 82
Coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
On Pk1​, O and O(−1) are line bundles, so each stalk of either is a free rank-one module over the local ring. Nevertheless their spaces of global sections are k and zero. Indeed a section of O(−1) on the two standard charts would require a polynomial a(t) to equal t−1b(t−1), which has only strictly negative powers. Only the zero section can satisfy this. Pointwise existence of unrelated stalk isomorphisms does not supply a morphism of sheaves.

Coherent ideal sheaf (I⊆OX​)

Words: 17
Coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
An ideal sheaf of a closed subscheme that is a coherent sheaf as a module over the structure sheaf. On a Noetherian scheme, every quasi-coherent ideal sheaf is coherent.

Finite twisting resolution of a coherent sheaf on projective space (0→⨁O(arj​)→⋯→⨁O(a0j​)→F→0)

Words: 57
Coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
A coherent sheaf on Pkn​ is the sheaf associated with a graded module for a finite graded k[t0​,…,tn​]-module. Choose a finite graded free resolution by the Hilbert syzygy theorem and sheafify it; exactness of localization preserves exactness. All terms are finite sums of twisting sheaves on projective space. Twisting sufficiently positively makes every term acyclic in positive degree, and dimension shifting in long exact sequences in sheaf cohomology proves Serre vanishing. The graded-module description is supplied by Stacks Project, Section 30.15.

Support dimension of a coherent sheaf (dimSuppF)

Words: 34
Coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
The support dimension is the dimension of a scheme of the closed support of a coherent sheaf. Tensoring with a line bundle leaves its support unchanged. Quotienting by a section that avoids its associated points reduces the support dimension by at least one.

Associated point of a coherent sheaf

Words: 61
Coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
An associated point of a coherent sheaf is a point whose corresponding prime is the annihilator of an element of the module on an affine chart. There are finitely many on a Noetherian scheme. A section of a line bundle avoiding them acts injectively on the sheaf, even when the scheme is nonreduced. Over an infinite field a sufficiently ample linear system supplies such a section.

Direct image of a coherent sheaf under a closed immersion

Words: 38
Coherent sheaf OurBigBook.com
If i:Z↪X is a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes and F is a coherent sheaf on Z, then i∗​F is coherent on X. Affine-locally this regards a finitely generated A/I-module as a finitely generated A-module.

Tensor product of sheaves (F⊗OX​​G)

Words: 29
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
The tensor product of two sheaves of OX​-modules is the sheafification of U↦F(U)⊗OX​(U)​G(U). Its stalk at x is Fx​⊗OX,x​​Gx​.

Direct image sheaf (f∗​F)

Words: 529 Articles: 10
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
For a continuous map f:X→Y and a sheaf F on X, the direct image is defined by (f∗​F)(V)=F(f−1V) for every open V⊆Y.
The direct image sheaf is the result of the direct image functor: (f∗​F)(V)=F(f−1V).

Derived direct image of sheaves (Rf∗​)

Words: 67 Articles: 1
Direct image sheaf OurBigBook.com
For a continuous map f:X→Y, the derived direct image Rf∗​ is obtained by applying f∗​ to an injective resolution. Composition with derived global sections gives RΓ(Y,Rf∗​E)≅RΓ(X,E).

Proper base change for sheaves ((Rf∗​E)y​≅RΓ(f−1(y),E))

Words: 37
Derived direct image of sheaves OurBigBook.com
For a proper map of locally compact spaces and a constructible complex E, the derived stalk satisfies (Rf∗​E)y​≅RΓ(f−1(y),E∣f−1(y)​). In particular (Rif∗​Q)y​≅Hi(f−1(y);Q). Properness is what prevents fibre cohomology from missing nearby sections.

Projective direct image need not preserve surjections

Words: 61
Direct image sheaf OurBigBook.com
For f:Pk1​→Speck, let D consist of 0 and infinity. Its ideal sheaf is O(−2), giving an exact coherent sequence 0→O(−2)→O→OD​→0. The map on global sections is the diagonal k→k⊕k, which is not surjective. Since direct image to the point is global sections, projectivity does not make direct image right exact.

Words: 81 Articles: 1
Sheaf cohomology OurBigBook.com
Coherent cohomology means sheaf cohomology with coefficients in a coherent sheaf. On a separated Noetherian scheme, a finite affine cover computes it using the Čech cochain complex, because intersections of affine opens are affine and positive-degree quasi-coherent sheaf cohomology vanishes there. Short exact sequences give long exact sequences in sheaf cohomology.

For a coherent sheaf F on a projective variety over a field, every Hq(X,F) is finite-dimensional, and Grothendieck vanishing gives zero for q>dimX. A closed embedding in projective space and a finite twisting resolution of a coherent sheaf on projective space reduce finiteness to the explicit cohomology of twisting sheaves on projective space. The same resolution proves Serre vanishing after sufficiently positive twisting.

A short exact sequence of cochain complexes of sheaves 0→E→F→G→0 induces ⋯→Hi(E)→Hi(F)→Hi(G)→Hi+1(E)→⋯. Taking stalks is exact, so the construction and exactness follow from the ordinary long exact sequence of cohomology of complexes at every stalk. The stalkwise connecting maps come from the lift-and-differentiate construction and form a sheaf morphism.

For a complex concentrated in degree zero it is ordinary sheaf cohomology. The relative de Rham complex uses this construction to compute fibre cohomology and its Hodge filtration.

Here U​F is the direct image from an open restriction. Lower local vanishing makes the edge map Hi(X,U​F)→Hi(U,F∣U​) injective. Local vanishing of a class alone does not imply global vanishing.

Under wi​=1/zi​ it is w1​w2​O(Cw2​), the entire functions divisible by both coordinates. This is an infinite-dimensional analytic vector space; restricting representatives to finite Laurent polynomials loses classes. The class of 1/(z1​z2​) is nonzero, so X is not a Stein manifold.

A coherent sheaf F on PN is r-regular if Hi(PN,F(r−i))=0 for every i>0. It is then (r+1)-regular and F(r) is globally generated. Persistence follows by induction with a hyperplane avoiding the associated points and its restriction exact sequence. A sheaf on an embedded projective scheme is tested after pushforward to projective space.

An injective resolution is an exact sequence starting with a sheaf and continuing with injective sheaves. It is constructed by successively embedding each quotient in an injective sheaf. The Euler characteristic of a coherent sheaf gives h0(O(A))≥degA+1−g. Every divisor of sufficiently large degree is therefore linearly equivalent to n0​P+E with E effective. The point-supported quotient for adding E transfers vanishing to that divisor. Torsion is first removed so that the relevant inclusions are injections of locally free sheaves.

If B is very ample, Serre vanishing for the finitely many fixed twists F(−iB) makes F⊗Lm zero-regular. Persistence of Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity gives all nonnegative B-twists. Its multiplication gives 0→F→F(aA)→Q→0, where Q has support dimension at most d−1. After tensoring with OX​(mN), the middle term has zero higher sheaf cohomology, uniformly in m. Sheaf cohomology OurBigBook.com
For a coherent sheaf on a Noetherian scheme, its sheaf cohomology vanishes in degrees greater than its support dimension. In particular, a zero-dimensional projective scheme has no positive-degree coherent cohomology.

Hi(X,F)≅Hi(Γ(X,A∙)).

A sheaf is flasque when every restriction map is surjective. Flasque sheaves are acyclic for global sections, so Hi(X,F)=0 for i>0.

Words: 66
Flasque sheaf OurBigBook.com
For a Noetherian ring A, an injective module I gives a flasque sheaf on SpecA. If U=SpecA∖V(a), clearing denominators on finitely many principal opens identifies Γ(U,I) with lim​n​HomA​(an,I). Each map extends to A by injectivity. Thus every section on U extends globally, and all restriction maps are surjective. This concerns sheafification of an injective module, rather than the different assertion that an injective sheaf of modules is flasque.

Flasque-kernel section-lifting lemma

Words: 97
Flasque sheaf OurBigBook.com
For a short exact sequence of sheaves with flasque sheaf kernel, every section of the quotient on any open set lifts to the middle sheaf on that set. Use the Zorn lemma to choose a maximal partial lift, with chains glued by the sheaf gluing axiom. A new local lift differs from the old one on their overlap by a kernel section. Extend that difference by flasqueness, adjust the new lift, and glue, contradicting maximality unless its domain is the entire open set. Consequently a quotient of two flasque sheaves is flasque. With an injective resolution of sheaves, the long exact sequence in sheaf cohomology and repeated dimension shifts prove that flasque sheaves have zero positive-degree cohomology.

Flasque resolution (0→F→I0→I1→⋯)

Words: 198 Articles: 1
Flasque sheaf OurBigBook.com
A flasque resolution is an exact sequence of sheaves of abelian groups whose terms Ij are flasque sheaves. Every such sheaf embeds by its section germs into the sheaf U↦∏P∈U​FP​. Its restriction maps are projections, so it is flasque. Apply this construction successively to the cokernels to obtain a resolution. The sheaf cohomology of F is the cohomology of the cochain complex Γ(X,I∙). A quotient of two flasque sheaves in a short exact sequence of sheaves is flasque: the flasque kernel allows local lifts to be glued into a section of the middle sheaf over the smaller open set; extend that lift using flasqueness of the middle sheaf, and project. Consequently the resolution's successive cokernels are flasque when F is flasque, and exactness of sections shows that all its positive-degree cohomology vanishes.
Godement resolution
Words: 74
Flasque resolution OurBigBook.com
Embed a sheaf of abelian groups F into the sheaf C(F)(U)=∏P∈U​FP​ by all its germs. Restrictions are projections, so C(F) is flasque. Repeat on the successive sheaf cokernels to obtain a canonical flasque resolution. Its complex of global sections computes sheaf cohomology. When F is itself flasque, the flasque-kernel section-lifting lemma makes every successive quotient flasque and makes the global-section complex exact in positive degrees, proving Hq(X,F)=0 for q>0 without assuming that vanishing in the construction.

For r≥1, a twisting sheaf on projective space has H0(Pkr​,O(n))=k[X0​,…,Xr​]n​ when n≥0, and top cohomology with basis the Laurent monomials of total degree n whose exponents are all negative. All intermediate sheaf cohomology vanishes. Their dimensions are (rn+r​) and (r−n−1​) respectively, with the top group nonzero only for n≤−r−1. Decompose the standard Čech cochain complex by exponent vector: no negative exponents gives a simplex with cohomology in degree zero; a nonempty proper negative-support set admits a contracting homotopy inserting a vertex outside that set; all negative exponents give only the top term. For r=0, every twist is trivial on Speck and has H0=k.

The two affine opens D(x),D(y) cover the punctured affine plane. Their intersection has ring k[x±1,y±1]. The Čech cohomology in degree one is the quotient by k[x±1,y]+k[x,y±1]. Its basis consists precisely of the Laurent monomials whose two exponents are negative, so this vector space is infinite-dimensional. Global functions, by contrast, form k[x,y].

Its Čech cochain complex is k[t]⊕k[t−1]→k[t,t−1], with map (a,b)↦tnb−a. The kernel has basis 1,t,…,tn for n≥0. The cokernel has basis tn+1,…,t−1 for n≤−2. The two-chart complex also proves vanishing in degrees at least two.

A frame on the infinity chart equals zn times a finite-chart frame. Entire finite-chart functions remove Laurent powers k≥0, and infinity-chart functions remove powers k≤n. The positive and negative tails converge to entire chart functions, so only the finite gap n<k<0 remains. Thus the first cohomology has basis zn+1,…,z−1 when n≤−2 and is zero when n≥−1. The same transition relation gives global sections of dimension max(n+1,0).

Čech cochain complex OurBigBook.com

Pairing an invertible sheaf with its differential-valued dual gives the perfect Serre duality pairing. Since the global regular functions on an integral projective curve over an algebraically closed field are k, evaluation at the constant function 1 identifies this trace canonically with an isomorphism to k.
